title: fix(objectql)!: a detail write asks the caller’s read door for its master-detail header — an unreadable header answers as a nonexistent one (#22519)
body:
Fixes #22519
Clause-②: no (narrowing)

Implements the maintainer's ruling 6107211425 (letter A) on #22519. A write of a master-detail detail whose header the caller cannot read now answers exactly what a write naming a header that exists nowhere answers. This holds for every detail, `controlled_by_parent` or not, on insert, update (a repoint included) and the bulk paths. System callers are unchanged. The plain `lookup` reference probe is not touched, and ADR-0055 is not edited.

## Mechanism (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`)

The write's master-detail header read now uses the two-read shape the preview already uses (`resolvePreviewParents`):

1. **`masterDetailHeadersCallerReads`** (new): the caller's read door. It is one `find` under the caller's own context, projected to `id`. One id is asked by equality and a batch by `$in`, which are the predicate shapes the elevated reads already send. A header it does not return binds as a missing header binds. That covers a header hidden by row scope, a refused read of the header object, and a failed read (logged once at `warn`). A system caller asks no read door.
2. The existing elevated, tenant-kept read (#19837), run only for the headers read 1 returned. A header the caller can read is still judged on its stored values, including a column that field-level security hides or masks for that caller. The preview's per-column masking stays the preview's own.

Every write path goes through three places, and each one takes the rule:

| Seat | Write paths it serves |
|:---|:---|
| `resolveMasterDetailParent` | update by id: the landing header, the header named during the FK-lock settlement, and the repoint's `previousParent` |
| `resolveMasterDetailParents` | `insert` (single and array), `insertMany` (which calls `insert`), and the predicate (bulk) update's landing and previous headers |
| `assertReferencesResolve` calls the new `masterDetailHeaderExists` | a field of type `master_detail` only, on insert, update by id and the predicate update. A `lookup` keeps `referenceExists`, unchanged |

How the write paths were enumerated: the engine's write methods are `insert`, `insertMany` and `update` (by id and predicate). `execute` and the scoped-context and transaction wrappers route into these. Every call site of the two resolvers and of the reference check was found with `grep`, and none is left on the old read.

**Docblocks.** The `resolveMasterDetailParent` paragraph that called the elevation "settled upstream" now states this rule. `resolveMasterDetailParents` and `assertReferencesResolve` gained the matching sections. Four comments described the write's header read as elevated-only, and each now says the write asks the read door too:
- the preview docblock;
- the `validate` docblock;
- the inline comment in `validate`;
- the `resolvePredicateRelated` docblock.

The preview's code is unchanged. Its read 2 calls `resolveMasterDetailParents`, which now asks the read door again, so a preview pays one extra id-projected query (see Acceptance notes).

## Pins (`engine-unreadable-master-detail-header.test.ts`, synthetic read scope as in #22474's preview pins)

Every refusal pin asserts the ADR-0112 envelope (`status` and `code`, plus the field code). It also asserts that the message, with the id taken out, matches the message for a nonexistent id.

- **(a) The reference check**, through four doors: insert, batch insert, repoint by id and bulk repoint. An unreadable header in either state answers `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` / `reference_not_found`, which is what a nonexistent id answers, and nothing is written. A refused read of the header object answers the same. In the partial `insertMany`, an unreadable row fails exactly as a nonexistent row does, while a readable row lands.
- **(b) `requiredWhen` over `parent`**: insert, update by id and bulk, and a repoint by id and in bulk. An unreadable header in either state answers what a nonexistent header answers (ADR-0137 D2's unevaluable refusal). A refused read of the header object answers the same.
- **(c) `readonlyWhen` over `parent`**, by id and in bulk: the field locks with the same drop report. Under `strictReadonlyWrites` the refusal is the same.
- **The mechanism:** the read door is asked first, then the elevated read, both for the binding and for the reference check.
- **Controls:**
  - a readable header is unchanged: locked requires, open lands, the lock holds or lets the field through;
  - a readable header whose state column the read door hides or masks is still judged on its stored value;
  - a nonexistent id answers as before;
  - a `controlled_by_parent` detail under a readable header is unchanged, and under an unreadable header it takes the same rule;
  - a system caller is unchanged: the header is bound whoever owns it, and no read door is asked;
  - a plain `lookup` to the same object keeps its elevated probe and asks no read door.

**Existing pins updated.** Each of these pinned the old read shape:
- `engine-reference-tenant-scope.test.ts`:
  - the tenancy-disabled master control now counts two finds;
  - the `group` posture control now counts two finds, each carrying the union;
  - the "header read runs ELEVATED" pin now asserts door, then elevated, for each read, with the tenant on all six.
- `engine-required-when-parent.test.ts`: the cost pin now counts one batched door read and one batched elevated read per insert, plus one door read per supplied header for the reference check.
- `validate-preview-parent.test.ts`: a header comment.

## Ablation (one-off proof, not kept as a test)

The ablation was run from committed `eefbde9b6c` through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, which restores the file on exit. It removed the read door by forcing `masterDetailHeadersCallerReads` to return every id: the anchor went from 1 to 0, and the blob from `513539a2e224` to `118559d7a44d`. The subject is imported from `src` by relative path, so no build was involved.

- **Mutated:** 22 failed and 81 passed across the four files. All 18 unreadable-header pins and the mechanism pin turned red, as did the 3 tenant-scope read-shape pins and the cost pin. **All 12 behaviour controls stayed green.**
- **Restored:** the blob equals HEAD (`513539a2e224`) and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

## Tests run

These ran on `bb5d7399d9` (the code before merging `origin/main`), then were re-scoped on the merged head `fef935481d`:

- `@objectstack/objectql` full `vitest run --project local`: **401 files / 7840 tests passed**.
- `@objectstack/plugin-security` full `vitest run` (its vitest aliases `@objectstack/objectql` to `src`, so the real `SecurityPlugin` rules ran against this change, the `controlled-by-parent-*` suites included): **196 files passed, 3973 passed / 45 skipped**.
- On `fef935481d`, after merging `origin/main`, rebuilding `@objectstack/objectql...` and running `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`:
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql typecheck` passed (`tsc --noEmit` and `check:test-typecheck`; the three edited or new test files are in the `tsconfig.test.json` program);
  - 11 targeted files passed (200 tests): the 4 files above plus the 7 whose test doubles first showed the single-id equality need.
- An earlier full run at `01ed9ca0e2` turned up 47 red tests in 7 files. In each of them, the test double's `find` handles flat equality but not `$in`. That is why one id is now asked by equality, which adds no driver-capability requirement beyond what the elevated reads already send.

**Gates, run on the head `fef935481d`.** The list comes from `dispatch-gates --commands`, re-derived on the real diff: 98 commands, the dispatch's 68 plus 30 that the docs-page edit adds. All 98 exited 0, and `--ran` reconciled 98 derived, 98 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED. One of them, `check-engine-split-ratio --days 90`, first exited 2 (a shallow-clone prerequisite). After `git fetch --shallow-since=2026-07-06 origin main` it exited 0. Each command and its exit code is in the report comment on #22519.

**Lint was narrowed, not skipped.** The repository-wide `pnpm lint` belongs to CI. Locally, `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` ran over the 5 changed `.ts` files and found 5 files, 0 errors and 0 warnings. That narrowing excludes nothing, for three reasons:
- the population comes from `eslint.config.mjs`, whose base block covers every `**/*.{ts,…}` file;
- the JSON output counted 5 files linted;
- the config never enables type-aware linting (it says so itself, no `parserOptions.project`), so this diff cannot change the verdict on any untouched file. The `.md` and `.mdx` changes are outside ESLint's file set.

## Acceptance notes

- **Outside the declared file surface: `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`** has one new row (29c) and its census counts regenerated by `pnpm gen:system-context-census`. `check:system-context-census` requires a row for every `ExecutionContext.isSystem` read, and the system-caller stand-down the ruling keeps is one new read. Without the row the gate stays red.
- **The ruling's invariant still has one gap, outside this PR's seam.** A one-hop predicate traversal through the master-detail FK goes through `resolvePredicateRelated`, which is the #18682 related read and its documented "accepted cost". For a tenanted master it still reads the header elevated, and its verdict comes before the reference check. So under such a rule, the answer for an unreadable header still depends on the header's stored state; a scratch probe confirmed this, and the probe was not committed. Handed to the seat as a finding: whether ruling A extends to the related read over the master-detail FK is a decision this PR does not take.
- **Cost:** one id-projected read under the caller's context per header resolution (once per batch), and one per supplied `master_detail` value in the reference check. A preview with a header pays one more id read, because its read 2 now carries the write's own read door. Carrier: none.
- **Line count:** 812 changed lines (+754 / −58) against the ruling's 300–600 estimate. The surplus is the pin file (496 lines) and the census row and counts.
- Reachability in real deployments was not measured. The ruling struck that step because the rule only tightens.
